summary: Linn County, OR lookout site on High Deck (Hurricane Deck) first manned in 1907; 1947 L-4 cab removed 1972; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: Platform tower and tent (1907), later a cabin; L-4 standard 14 x 14 cab with cement foundation and catwalk, built 1947
facts.status_note: L-4 cab removed in 1972; no source describes what remains on the site today
facts.agency: Linn County Fire Patrol association (Linn FPA)

events.note: Platform tower and tent, per the register; Forest Lookouts repeats the 1907 date
Forest Lookouts calls it the first lookout manned in that part of Oregon
Two lightning fires seen from the lookout after dark; the valley patrolman was called by telephone and the fires were put out
Patrolman stationed at the lookout in August 1912
Cupola-style lookout house, per Forest Lookouts; the register dates cabin living quarters to 1920 instead
Cabin living quarters added, per the Former Fire Lookout Sites register
J.A. Duncan at the lookout for the summer
Hill Fire Patrol fire near Sodaville, reported from Hurricane Deck and Green Peter lookouts, put out before much damage
J.A. Duncan back at the lookout for the season
Fay Miller, keeper for the Hill Fire Patrol, taken ill in September and helped down the trail
Spring went dry; nearest water at Cascadia; a pack horse was expected to be needed
Old lookout unusable; new 14 x 14 standard L-4 cab with full cement foundation and catwalk

resolved_conflicts.field: date of first house or cabin
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Former Fire Lookout Sites entry says cabin living quarters were added in 1920; Forest Lookouts dates a cupola-style lookout house to 1919. Both dates are kept as reported and the story says the sources disagree.

notes_for_editor: Brief record checks out: status gone, 2011 FFLOS registration, Linn FPA administration and elevation all match the register; no corrections. The 1919 (Forest Lookouts) versus 1920 (register) house date is a genuine conflict and is reported as such. Nothing read describes remains on the site or public access, so the story says no source describes the site today and access is left unrated. facts.staffing 'as_of 1947' reads the Forest Log statement that the station had been manned each year since 1907; it is not a current status. No photos added: the Forest Lookouts photo credits name a 1946 Oregon Department of Forestry collection and John McWade, but no licence was visible. Budget: 2 searches and 6 page reads (the cherylhill.net standing-lookouts list was checked but not used).
